ParcelwiseHelp centre

Answers, before you have to ask.

The eighteen questions our support desk hears most, written by the people who answer them. Searched 41,280 times last month.

The 8 most-asked of 18 answers

How are shipping rates calculated?

Rates come straight from each carrier’s commercial tariff, then your plan discount is applied: 12% on Starter, 21% on Growth. You see the final price before you buy a label, and nothing is added afterwards.

Rates & labels
Can I print labels on a thermal printer?

Yes. Every label downloads as a 4×6 in PDF or a ZPL file, so any 203 or 300 dpi thermal printer works. A4 and Letter sheets with two labels per page are there too.

Rates & labels
What happens if I buy a label and never use it?

Void it from the shipment page within 30 days and the full amount returns to your balance, usually within 2 business days. A label a carrier has already scanned can’t be voided, so you’re only refunded for parcels that never moved.

Rates & labels
Can I create labels in bulk?

Upload a CSV or select up to 500 orders at once. Parcelwise picks the cheapest service that still meets each order’s delivery promise and prints the whole batch as one merged PDF.

Rates & labels
How accurate are the delivery estimates?

Over the last 90 days, 94.2% of parcels arrived on or before the date shown at checkout. Estimates come from each carrier’s scan history for that exact pair of postcodes, not a national average.

Rates & labels
Do you fill in customs forms for me?

Yes. CN22 and CN23 customs declarations and commercial invoices are built from each product’s HS code, weight and value, then sent electronically wherever the carrier accepts paperless customs.

International
Which countries can I ship to?

212 destinations. Some carriers restrict lithium batteries and perfume on certain routes; we flag those at checkout rather than letting the parcel come back to you three weeks later.

International
Who pays import duties?

You decide per store. Delivered Duty Paid charges your customer at checkout and we remit the duties for you; Delivered Duty Unpaid leaves them to be settled with the courier on arrival.

International
What is an HS code, and do I need one?

A six-to-ten digit tariff code that tells customs what is inside the box. Any parcel leaving the customs union needs one; our classifier suggests a code from the product title and you confirm it once.

International
How do return labels work?

Switch on the returns portal and customers create their own label from an order number and postcode. You’re charged when a return label is first scanned by the carrier, never when it is created.

Returns
Can I limit which items can be returned?

Set a return window in days, exclude product tags such as final-sale, and require a photo before a damaged-item claim goes through. Rules apply per store.

Returns
Is there a fee for the returns portal?

It’s included on Growth and costs €9 a month on Starter. Each return label is billed at the same discounted rate as an outbound label.

Returns
What if a parcel is lost or damaged?

Open a claim from the tracking page. We handle the carrier paperwork and refund the declared value up to €100 automatically, or up to €2,500 with Parcel Cover.

Returns
Is there a monthly fee?

Starter is free for your first 50 labels each month, then €0.05 per label. Growth is €29 a month with unlimited labels, the 21% carrier discount and the returns portal included.

Account & billing
Can several people share one account?

Invite as many teammates as you like and give each one a role: Owner, Shipper or Viewer. Shippers can buy labels but never see card or billing details.

Account & billing
What are the API rate limits?

100 requests per second in production and 10 in the sandbox. Batch endpoints accept up to 500 shipments per call and count as a single request.

Account & billing
Is there a sandbox for testing?

Every account has one. Test carriers return realistic tracking events, so you can build and test your API integration end to end without buying a single label.

Account & billing
How do I cancel?

Downgrade or close the account from Settings › Plan whenever you like. Any unused balance is refunded to the original card within 5 business days.

KILNWORKSClay, glaze & firing. Unit 4, Mill Yard

Questions we get asked at the counter

20 answers / 4 sections / Sep 2026

Still stuck? Ring the kiln room on 0161 496 0734, Tue–Sat 10:00–18:00.

Orders

Dispatch, collection, shipping and returns.

How fast do you dispatch?

Orders placed before 13:00 leave the same day, Monday to Friday. Clay is heavy, so anything over 20 kg travels on a two-day pallet service.

Can I collect from the studio?

Yes. Choose Collect at checkout and we text you when it’s on the shelf, usually within 2 hours. Collection is free.

What does shipping cost?

£4.90 under 5 kg, £9.50 up to 25 kg, and free on orders over £120. Pallets of clay are quoted per bag.

Do you ship outside the UK?

Tools and glazes go to the EU and Norway. Clay doesn’t: it’s too heavy to send at a price anyone would pay.

Can I return opened clay?

Unopened bags within 30 days, yes. Once a bag is open it can’t come back, but tools and unused glaze can.

Firing

Booking kiln space, prices and temperatures.

How do I book kiln space?

Leave work on the drop-off shelf, Tuesday to Saturday before 16:00. We bisque on Mondays and glaze on Thursdays.

What does a firing cost?

90p per litre of shelf space for bisque and £1.20 for glaze. A typical mug takes about 0.6 litres: 54p to bisque, 72p to glaze.

What temperatures do you fire to?

Bisque to 1000 °C. Glaze firings are cone 6, about 1222 °C, in an oxidising electric kiln. We don’t do reduction.

What if my piece breaks in the kiln?

If it’s our fault the firing is free and we’ll tell you. Most cracks come from thick bases or damp clay, and we’ll show you where.

How long until I get my work back?

Seven days for bisque, ten for glaze. We text you the moment it reaches the collection shelf.

Clay & glaze

What to buy, what’s food-safe, how to store it.

Which clay should I start with?

Our buff stoneware, KW-12. It’s forgiving on the wheel, fires from cone 4 to 8, and a 12.5 kg bag makes about twenty mugs.

Are your glazes food-safe?

Every glaze marked FS is lab-tested for lead and cadmium release at cone 6. Unmarked glazes are for decorative surfaces only.

Can I bring my own glaze?

If it’s cone 6, comes with a data sheet and you’ve tested it on a tile first. A runny glaze ruins a kiln shelf, and those are £85 each.

How should I store clay?

Sealed, cool and above freezing: frozen clay turns crumbly. Wrap a damp cloth inside the bag every couple of months.

Do you sell reclaimed clay?

Yes, pugged studio reclaim at £6 per 10 kg bag. It’s a blend of stonewares, so throw a test piece first.

Studio

Classes, wheel hire and membership.

Do you run classes?

Six-week wheel courses start every month, eight people a class, £240 including 12.5 kg of clay and all your firings.

Can I rent a wheel by the hour?

£9 an hour or £60 for a ten-hour card, Tuesday to Saturday. First come, first served; members get priority.

Is the studio accessible?

Step-free from the street, with a height-adjustable wheel and an accessible toilet. Ask and we’ll keep the low bench free for you.

What’s included in membership?

Round-the-clock access, your own shelf, 30 litres of firing a month and 10% off everything. £85 a month, cancel any time.

Can I bring children?

Over-12s can join an adult on the wheel. Saturday mornings are family sessions for ages 6 and up.

html:
LarchmoorA residency for writers & translators

Before you apply

Eight questions, answered at length, because a residency is a large decision. Read straight through, or jump from the index.

Applications for 2027 close 30 NovemberStart an application

01

Who is the residency for?

Writers and literary translators working on a book-length project, in any language, at any stage after the first chapter. You don’t need a publisher or an agent. You do need to be able to show us twenty pages.

We read every application blind. Names, prizes and publications are removed before the panel sees a single word.

02

How long is a stay, and when?

Four, six or eight weeks, in three seasons: February to March, May to June, and September to October. Each season houses nine residents.

You choose the length when you apply. Most first-time residents pick six weeks, long enough to change a book and short enough to keep the rest of a life.

03

What does it cost?

Nothing. Your room, studio and meals are covered, and we pay a stipend of £350 a week for the costs of being away. For a six-week stay that is £2,100.

We also reimburse travel: up to £400 within Europe, or up to £900 from further afield. Receipts, not estimates.

04

Can my partner or family come too?

Not to stay, I’m afraid. The houses are built for nine people working quietly. Visitors are welcome on Sundays, and the inn in the village keeps two rooms at a residency rate.

05

What will my days look like?

Mornings are protected: no events, no visits, breakfast left out until eleven. Dinner is together at seven, cooked by Maren, who has run the kitchen since 2014.

Twice a season a visiting editor offers one-to-one sessions. They are optional, and so is everything else except dinner.

06

Is the house accessible?

Three of the nine studios are on the ground floor, with step-free access, a wet room and a level path to the dining hall. Tell us what you need on the form; it never reaches the panel and never affects their decision.

07

How are residents chosen?

A panel of three, changed every year, reads the anonymised applications in two rounds. Last year 1,140 people applied for 27 places, about one in forty-two.

The panel looks for a book that will be different because of the time here, not for the most polished sample.

08

When will I hear back?

Applications for the 2027 seasons close on 30 November 2026. Everyone hears by 31 January, by email, whatever the answer.

We can’t give individual feedback, but we publish the panel’s notes on what made the shortlist, and they are worth reading before you start.

That’s everything. Still wondering about something? Write to Ilse at the house; she answers every letter herself.
